source_observations.finding: The c.e. definition explicitly includes the empty set, but in proving c.e. implies domain of a partial computable function the frozen proof immediately assumes S is the range of a total computable function. No such function from naturals has empty range, so the empty case is omitted.

source_observations.finding: The frozen theorem allows empty c.e. sets, but its first two proofs immediately assume that each of A and B is the range of a total computable enumerator. The empty set has no such enumerator. The second proof explicitly handles an empty intersection, but it still assumes total enumerators for A and B before that step.
source_observations.action: State before those two proofs that either empty input set makes the intersection empty and the union the other c.e. set, then use total enumerators only for the nonempty case. Add adjacent reader note OLCMP-019; preserve every source formula and identifier.
